recipes.name: Roasted Pork Chops with Tomatoes, Mushrooms, and Garlic Sauce

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).

In a 9x13 inch baking dish, toss tomatoes, mushrooms, garlic, and olive oil with salt and pepper to taste. Mix lightly with hands to coat all ingredients with oil, and spread the tomato-mushroom mixture to the edges of the dish, leaving the center free for the pork chops.

Combine 1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, cumin, ground coriander, oregano, marjoram, thyme, rosemary, sage, basil, garlic powder, onion powder, ground paprika, sugar, and crushed red pepper in a bowl to make a spice rub.
Sprinkle the pork chops with the spice rub, working the rub well into both sides of the meat. Place pork chops in the center of the baking dish, surrounded by the tomato and mushroom mixture.

Roast in preheated oven until the pork is no longer pink in the center and mushrooms are tender, about 45 to 50 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of a chop should read 145 degrees F (63 degrees C). Transfer pork chops to a serving dish and top with roasted tomato-mushroom mixture and all pan juices to serve.

review.reviewBody: Fabulous recipe! I used the Italian Herb and Soul Seasoning blends instead of mixing my own, as the cook's note suggests. I also added red onion as suggested by another reviewer. My own twist came with adding chunks of summer squash to the vegetables. My absolute favorite part of the dish was the flavor of the roasted veggies. This is definitely a keeper!

AWESOME! Thank you for another way to get some vegetables into my husband and he LOVED it. My modifications: 1 lb of boneless chops, 2 zucchini, 1 pkg mushrooms and 1 big tomato. Chopped up all the veggies put them in a bowl together and tossed them with olive oil, salt, pepper and Italian seasoning. Put them around the outside of the pan. Seasoned the chops with seasoning salt, Italian seasoning and Mrs. Dash Garlic and Herb. This combo covered most of the seasonings except the red pepper which we didn't want anyway. Because I had much less meat, I cooked mine at 350 for the first 30 minutes and 425 for the last 15 to keep from overcooking. It was perfect. Served it over brown rice with a sprinkling of parmesan cheese over the top. My veggie averse husband asked me to put it in our regular rotation. Leftovers today were even better!

This is an excellent recipe! Followed it exactly the first time and everyone loved it. I've made it several more times and it turns out great. I had to use canned plum tomatoes once instead of fresh tomatoes and the recipe was still delicious. Last time I made it, I added onions, zucchini, carrots, and red bell pepper chunks. I think that heightened the flavors even more. The best thing is, this dish can sit in the oven warming while not drying out the pork. The pork is always juicy. Thanks for a keeper!

This is 5 Star quality. I used all the spices, didn't have a couple, but threw in a couple of 1/4 tsps. Italian Seasoning. Followed all to the letter, except did use regular tomatoes since did not have Romas, and sliced the mushrooms I did have on hand, white, small portos, and a couple of Shitakes. 
Added red onion, the little I had left from another dish, as others have suggested/
This was delicious. The sauce that cooks down as the dish cooks, the rub, OMGosh, this tasted like I was eating in a fine-dining restaurant.
Make sure you cover it...I think that's why one poster's burned dry. Always good to put in directions whether to cover it or not. I wasn't going to, because it didn't say to, but figured it out after reading comments.
Loved it. So did Hubs. YUM

The rub for this recipe emptied about a third of my spice cabinet, but it was oh so good! 
I only had two roma tomatoes, so I used some tomatillos from my garden. Those and the diced sweet onion that I added gave it just a little more zip. Not spiciness, but a mildly tangy flavor. 
I'll make this again and again. The rub mixture is something I'll also try on other meats, such as chicken.

The mushrooms and tomatoes were divine!! I would've given it 5-stars if it weren't for the effort of yanking all of those spices out for the rub that ended up tasting just like, well, spicy. All of those complex flavors just didn't come together the way that I would've anticipated. But baked at 350 deg. for 35, 40 min., the chops and veggies were the perfect texture and done-ness for my family, and we will gladly do this recipe again, but maybe w/ a simplified rub, or my simple go-to for pork chops - sea salt, black pepper, paprika, and EVOO. Very good dish that I'm glad to have tried!

Great recipe! I read over the crushed red pepper so it didn't get added but it was still great without. I do however recommend reducing the cook time by 5-10 minutes if using a standard chop. The recipe does not specify thickness or bone in/out and mine were overdone. Overall good recipe!

Have made this several times and we love it! Didn't have quite all the spices on hand that were called for , so omitted a few. Also my pork chops were thin cut so I turned down the oven to 400 degrees and reduced the cooking time to 35 minutes.

This was a great pork chop recipe. But I think 40+ minutes at 425 is way too long. I cooked it at 400 for 40 minutes and they were overdone.
I added onions and bell peppers to the veggie mix, and they were delicious. I did the spice rub exactly as written.

Absolutely delicious! I used italian seasoning and then added the rest of the spices to save time. I added fresh greens beans and sliced baby carrots to the mix. It was a total hit. Im making it for the second time as we speak and cant WAIT for dinner!
We loved the recipe - so very easy, too! I used a spice mix I had in the house that had almost everything listed, so it was extremely easy for me! This will be in our rotation.
I followed the recipe just didn’t include some of the spices because we didn’t have them. The rub turned out great! The veggies were delicious with it and the sauce was amazing!
Easy tasty and I loved it
Done right the mushrooms and tomatoes are delicious.

Absolutely delicious! Only thing I would do is cut down the. Ookimg time for the pork chops, or use thicker cut ones, as they were a bit dry. The sauce, and the flavors of the herb mixture were just fabulous and I will be sure to make it again.
Yummy, savory, juicy. The whole family really enjoyed it.
Wow a lot of great flavor! Easy recipe.

we really enjoyed this.. and it was so easy that bf was even able to pull it off.. idk if i'd want to try the cheat with the italian seasoning and the soul seasoning.. we basically had everything the recipe called for and i believe i asked him to leave out the thyme.. ty so much for the recipe
Absolutely wonderful!! Had lots of flavor.
Very good. Don't forget to cover it when you put it in the oven!!
